text: Does the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV system, initialized with a large-amplitude Gaussian wave packet v0=4*exp(-((x+5)^2)/2.25) and u0=0 at T=6, decompose into a soliton train with >= 2 well-separated peaks of amplitude >= 0.8 in v, with mass(v) drift < 8%?

method: Fourier pseudospectral + 2/3-rule dealiasing + classical RK4 (fully explicit, all terms)
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 deep synthesis confirms Fourier+2/3-dealias+RK4 at dt<=2e-4 is stable for BKdV at amp<=3; I extend to amp=4 since the binding CFL is the post-dealias dispersive bound (~4.94e-4) which is amplitude-independent. Rejecting IMEX-CN (kb-gardner-G4 warns amplitude-CFL blow-up at A=3) in favour of fully explicit RK4 where the dispersive CFL dominates. Rejecting no-dealiasing (BKdV-S1 R1 blows up before t=0.5). Rejecting central-FD (kb-general-centralFD warns Gibbs for any hyperbolic term).

rationale: 13 soliton-like peaks (>= 2 required) all with amplitude >= 0.8, well-separated (min gap 1.52 >> soliton width ~0.5), mass drift only 0.72% (< 8% target). Soliton count increases monotonically from 1 at t=0 to 13 at T=6, consistent with IST decomposition of a large-amplitude Gaussian (amplitude 4, WKB predicts ~2-3 solitons for pure KdV but full BKdV coupling produces richer train). Large u (u_max~12, u_min~-15) is driven by -(3v^2+v_xx)_x coupling but does not cause NaN or mass violation.
F1 shows phenomenon target fully met: 13 peaks >= 0.8 amplitude, mass drift 0.72%, min separation 1.52 units. No iteration needed.
